title: SvidSigner::sign_jwt_svid takes untyped serde_json::Value and hardcodes a 300s TTL
description:
hire-core/src/signer.rs:92-113.

TTL: `exp: now + 300` is baked into the function body with no parameter and no constant. A caller cannot issue a shorter-lived token for a high-assurance audience or a longer one for a batch job. The audience extension model already accepts `hire_max_age` (hire-core/src/audience.rs:25) but there is no way to plumb it into token lifetime. Adding a `ttl` argument later breaks every caller; adding it now costs nothing.

Claims: `hire_ext: serde_json::Value` accepts any JSON at all. The crate already defines the intended type — `HireClaims` in the same crate (hire-core/src/hvid.rs:24) — and the signature declines to use it. The result is visible at hire-grpc/src/service.rs:162-173, where the claims are assembled as an ad-hoc `json!` literal that has already drifted from `HireClaims` (filed separately). Taking `&HireClaims` (or `impl Serialize`) would have made that drift a compile error.

Secondary, same signature: `audiences: &[&str]` forces every caller holding a `Vec<String>` to allocate a throwaway `Vec<&str>` first — service.rs:176 does exactly that. `impl IntoIterator<Item = impl AsRef<str>>` costs the same and removes the boilerplate.

Also undocumented on this public method: the `exp`/`iat` claim semantics, that `aud` is emitted as an array even for a single audience, and that `sub` and `spiffe_id` are both set to the same input string (signer.rs:103,107) — a caller cannot tell which one verifiers are supposed to trust.
